framework.reasoning: The paper's core artifact is a parameterized quantum circuit executed via Qiskit (qiskit-aer for simulation, qiskit-ibm-runtime SamplerV2 for hardware) -- this is the mandatory quantum SDK dependency and is not itself one of the schema's three framework choices. For the classical side (parameter optimisation of the few circuit angles theta, and the two-parameter affine post-processing layer of Theorem 3.15), the paper reports Adam as one of three optimisation methods, which is most naturally implemented with a lightweight PyTorch autograd wrapper around the Qiskit-computed probabilities; L-BFGS-B (Method A) uses scipy.optimize directly and does not require a DL framework at all. Per the Architecture Planner's own default rule (Section 1: 'Default to PyTorch if unspecified'), PyTorch is selected as the nominal classical framework label, used only for Method C (Adam) and for the differentiable affine correction layer; Methods A and B are implemented with scipy/numpy directly. JAX/TensorFlow were not mentioned in the paper and offer no stated advantage here, so were not selected. No GPU/CUDA is required: the circuits are tiny (5-8 qubits), and even AerSimulator runs are CPU-feasible; GPU support for qiskit-aer is an optional, not required, acceleration path.

risk_assessment.description: Optimizer hyperparameters (learning rate, iteration/convergence budget) for all three methods (L-BFGS-B, two-stage, Adam) are unspecified in the paper (SIR training_pipeline confidence 0.45), so the generated trainer's default values are guesses that may not reproduce the paper's reported MAE/RMSE figures.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Expose all optimizer hyperparameters via config.yaml with clear ASSUMED comments; make QNNTrainer.fit_method_c_adam accept lr/betas as overridable arguments; add a config_debug.yaml with a small iteration budget for fast smoke-testing without claiming fidelity to the paper's exact numbers.

risk_assessment.description: The readout error probability p used in the hardware bound (Eq. 4.4, Proposition 3.20) is not present in the Appendix A hardware parameter table, yet it is required to reproduce the reported $18.578 total bound and 10/10 within-bound hardware validation.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Treat readout_p as a required, explicitly-flagged config field (ASSUMED, currently 0.01) rather than a hardcoded constant; document in README that this value must be replaced with live ibm_fez calibration data (available via qiskit-ibm-runtime backend properties) before claiming to reproduce Section 4.5's numbers.

risk_assessment.description: The exact loss-function normalisation constant (Section 4.1) is ambiguous due to PDF-extraction corruption; using the wrong constant would rescale gradients but not change the optimum, so risk to final theta is low, but any reported absolute loss values would not match the paper.
risk_assessment.source: SIR mathematical_spec item 'Training loss (mean-squared error)' (confidence 0.5); SIR ambiguities[0]
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement QNNMSELoss with the normalisation constant as a config-exposed multiplier (default 1/(2n)); add a unit test confirming the argmin over theta is invariant to the choice of constant.

risk_assessment.description: The exact gate-level Uniformly Controlled Rotation (UCR) decomposition of U(theta,x) is delegated to an external reference ([23], Moettoenen et al.) and not reproduced in the paper; an incorrect or non-equivalent decomposition would change the circuit's two-qubit gate count and hence lambda_U, silently invalidating the hardware bound.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use Qiskit's built-in UCRZGate/UCRYGate (or equivalent) primitives directly rather than a hand-rolled decomposition, and add a circuit-equivalence unit test against the naive multi-controlled-gate implementation (as the paper itself does in Section 4.1.1, tolerance 1e-9) before trusting derived lambda_U values.

risk_assessment.description: The value of n0 (padding offset between accuracy blocks n and qubit count, n = ceil(log2(4n+n0))) used in the main numerical experiments is not explicitly stated; Remark 3.14's simplification (n0=0) is assumed but not confirmed for the hardware run.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Expose n0 as a config field defaulting to 0; add an assertion in QNNCircuitBuilder that raises a clear error if the configured n_qubits is inconsistent with ceil(log2(4*n_accuracy_blocks+n0)), so any silent mismatch surfaces immediately rather than producing subtly wrong results.

risk_assessment.description: Hardware execution requires live IBM Quantum access to ibm_fez (Heron r2) and its calibration data; this is not guaranteed to be available or stable over time (queue times, backend retirement, changing calibration).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Make run_hardware.py backend-name configurable and gracefully fall back to AerSimulator with a NoiseModel built from the paper's Table 1 constants (or live-fetched calibration via qiskit-ibm-runtime) if hardware access is unavailable.
